item.title: Why Your 0DTE Option Shows a Loss the Second You Buy It
item.description: Your fill was the ask, but your platform marks the open position at the mid. That gap, roughly half the spread, is the red you see before price moves.

item.title: Position Sizing for 0DTE
item.description: On 0DTE, position sizing is survival math: assume any trade can go to zero and size so a losing streak can't end you. Fixed-fractional risk beats gut-feel every.

item.description: Same-day options and intraday execution: timing, decay, and the mechanics of a fast tape.

item.description: A scalper sits flat most of the session, so a large cash balance can earn short-term interest while rates are positive. Small, riskless, easy to overlook.

item.title: Why 0DTE Bid-Ask Spreads Widen Into the Close (and What It Costs You)
item.description: As a 0DTE option nears expiration, market makers face soaring gamma risk and pull liquidity, so bid-ask spreads widen right when you may need to exit.

item.title: 0DTE vs 1DTE: Which to Trade?
item.description: 0DTE options give maximum gamma and brutal theta, all resolved by the close. 1DTE gives a premium cushion and room to breathe — at the cost of overnight risk.

item.title: 0DTE vs Swing Trading: Speed vs Patience
item.description: 0DTE trading is intraday, fast, and decay-driven with no overnight risk; swing trading holds positions for days to weeks, riding larger moves. Here's the difference.

item.title: 0DTE vs Weeklies: Which Should a Beginner Start With?
item.description: 0DTE options are cheap and fast but decay brutally; weekly options give more time and are more forgiving.

item.title: The 1-Minute vs. 5-Minute Chart for 0DTE: Which Timeframe Leads
item.description: For 0DTE scalping, the 5-minute chart sets the structure and trend while the 1-minute times the entry.

item.title: The 1DTE Morning Exit: Managing a Position You Bought Yesterday
item.description: If you carried a 1DTE overnight, the next morning is the whole game — the open reveals the gap, and you have one session of time value left.

item.title: The 1DTE Overnight Hold: When Carrying Risk Overnight Makes Sense
item.description: Holding to tomorrow buys back some time value but hands you gap risk and weekend decay. What the thesis has to look like before that swap is worth making.

item.title: 1DTE SPY Scalp Mechanics

item.title: Absorption on the Tape: When Heavy Selling Doesn't Move Price
